newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sets power plant tenders for July.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sets power plant tenders for July.

text.p: Hungary's electricity supplier MVM said on Monday it would invite bids in July for 2000 megawatts of new Hungarian capacity.
It said plans for two new 500 megawatt plants announced earlier in the day by the German consortium RWE Energie AG and EVS AG were part of the 2000 megawatt programme.

"There will be two closed tenders for 1,000 MW each, the first for smaller units and the second for larger plants which have a longer lead-in time," MVM's strategic director Istvan Bakacs told Reuters.

The tender for smaller capacity plants of 20 to 200 MW will be for commissioning between 2001 and 2003 while the second tender will be for larger units to go on line between 2003 and 2005, Bakacs said.
He said the siting of the new plants will be for the bidders to suggest but acknowledged that RWE had already said it would bid in the second of the two tenders.

RWE director Klaus Bussfeld told Reuters earlier it would bid to build two new 500 MW power plants at the Matra power plant site it runs in north east Hungary, provided current drawn-out talks on energy pricing were resolved.

Bakacs said it was likely that the two July tenders would include a clause saying that no one firm would be able to own and operate more than 30 percent of Hungary's total capacity, which currently stands at 7,500 MW.
"Even if RWE wins the tender for two 500 MW units, with the other 800 MW it already operates it will still be inside the limit," he said.

Bakacs added that MVM will publish the invitation to tender in mid-July and the preliminary bids should be received by mid-September. This will be followed by a negotiation stage of five months, with the whole process expected to take around nine months.

The Matra investment programme represents one of the biggest foreign investments RWE has been involved in and the largest such programme in any of the ten countries applying to join the European Union (EU), the company said earlier.

Earlier on Monday, British generator Powergen Plc said it had secured a long-term power purchase agreement in Hungary, paving the way for the development of a 160 million pound ($261 million) power plant in Budapest.
